items.title: PrismML Squeezes an Agentic Coding Model into 5.9 GB with Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B
items.summary: PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B on Nov 24, an Apache 2.0 update to its ternary-quantized Qwen3.8 27B derivative that keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint while targeting multi-turn tool use and long agent runs. In the company's whitepaper, SWE-bench Verified rises from 60.8 to 75.6 (full-precision base: 80.6), Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 52.8 to 60.1, and AppWorld from 51.2 to 90.5. The model reaches 291 tokens/s on an H100 with multi-token prediction and about 204 tokens/s on a consumer RTX 4090; it runs via llama.cpp on NVIDIA/Intel GPUs and MLX on Mac, iPhone and iPad.
items.impact: It pushes genuinely useful agentic coding onto consumer hardware and private repositories, where sensitive code never has to leave the device. The trade-off is real: all numbers are vendor-run, and LiveCodeBench v6 slipped slightly (83.8 to 83.0), so the 'near full-precision' claim needs outside testing.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Shows the Coding Harness Can Move Cost 5.4x While Score Barely Budges
items.summary: On Nov 24 the independent evaluator added Harness Comparisons to its Coding Agent Index v2.1, holding the model and reasoning effort fixed while swapping the agent harness across 13 options. GPT-6 Luna scored highest in OpenAI's Codex (25.9) and lowest in Qwen Code (17.2), while GLM-5.3-Flash peaked in Claude Code (38.9) and ranked last in Codex (27.8) - nine of 13 harnesses shifted three or more places between the two models. Cost per task varied far more than score: $0.11 to $0.62 for Luna and $0.38 to $0.91 for GLM-5.3-Flash. In first-turn replays, Codex's exec_command tool definition alone induced terse, telegraphic reasoning in 12 of 12 samples; Claude Code's tools did so in 0 of 11.
items.impact: Buying a coding agent is a model-plus-harness decision, and the wrapper can dominate the bill. It also suggests tool schemas themselves shape model reasoning, a design lever most teams do not measure. Caveats: only two models, one effort setting, default configurations and a small task suite.

items.title: Anthropic Turns MCP Servers into Skill Distributors as Tasks and Elicitation Go GA
items.summary: Anthropic opened Skills over MCP to public beta on Nov 24 in Claude and Claude Code: an MCP server can now ship step-by-step playbooks and best practices alongside its tools, loaded only when needed and updated with the server. Shopify uses them for store design and HubSpot for customer onboarding. Two protocol features reached general availability - Tasks, which lets a server run long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user confirmation (GitHub requires typing a repo name before deletion; Supabase confirms paid-project costs). File Uploads is coming next. Anthropic reports over 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads; the beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra.
items.impact: The agent toolchain is standardizing beyond tool calls into instructions, async work and human checkpoints - useful for anyone wiring agents into enterprise systems. The same flexibility is an attack surface: researchers found malicious agent skills after about 1.7 million installs in August, so skill provenance deserves the same scrutiny as package dependencies.

items.title: BAAI Launches REAL, a Physical-AI Benchmark That Finds Even Leaders Barely Above Half
items.summary: At its REAL Physical AI Open Day on Nov 24, BAAI published an evaluation system spanning 5 capability domains, 14 dimensions, 55 capabilities and 158 metrics, linked across benchmark, simulation and real-robot tracks, plus four first leaderboards. Kling 4.0 led the world-model board at 53.32 (closed models averaged 48.7, open models 30.3; best open model MiniMax H3 placed eighth). Gemini 4 Argon topped embodied reasoning at 75, with the top three all closed general models and the best dedicated embodied model, RynnBrain1.1-122B-A10B, at 18th. pi0.5 led simulated manipulation (59.83) and InternVLA-A1.5 real-robot manipulation (66.56). Science understanding averaged 83.8 but short-term memory only 37.8. BAAI also released the Innata-0 world system, Physis-V1-Preview, a 12,500-hour first-person HumanCOIN dataset sample and a human-centric safety whitepaper. Results were published by BAAI and not independently reproduced.
items.impact: This is the first attempt at a unified, deployment-oriented yardstick for physical AI, and the numbers puncture demo-driven narratives: spatial and physical reasoning remain weak and memory is a glaring bottleneck. The accompanying REAL Olympics, built with logistics, auto, home-appliance and manufacturing partners, shifts the test from staged tasks to real operating conditions.

items.title: Waymo Recalls 4,400+ Robotaxis After 11 Incursions into Closed Freeway Lanes
items.summary: NHTSA filings disclosed this week show Waymo filed two voluntary recalls on Nov 19 covering more than 4,400 vehicles with fifth- and sixth-generation driver systems. Between Oct 1 and Nov 6, eight robotaxis entered freeway areas closed by cones, construction or California Highway Patrol traffic breaks; a few days after Waymo deployed a fix, three more entered a construction site. Only two of the 11 incidents had been public. The California DMV banned Waymo from state freeways on Nov 11, citing an imminent hazard and saying the ban stays until effective corrective action is demonstrated. Waymo says no collisions or injuries occurred and that it runs six million driverless miles a week.
items.impact: Even the most mature autonomous fleet still fails on dynamic, human-controlled edge cases - cones, construction layouts and police gestures - which is exactly the long tail that matters for deploying robots in the physical world. The regulator's willingness to suspend operations also shows that aggregate safety statistics do not substitute for handling rare scenarios correctly.
